desc: Precompute `next[i]` = smallest j ≥ i+1 with A[j] ≥ 2·A[i] (or N+1 if none) using O(N) two-pointer sweep.
For each query [L,R], run greedy: pointer j starts at L; iterate i from L to R, set j = max(j, next[i]); if j > R break; else increment count and set j = j+1.
Read N, sorted array A, Q, queries; output each answer on its own line.
Verify correctness on both provided sample inputs.
Analyze worst-case total operations: for array 1,2,...,N and Q full-range queries, estimate per-query cost and total runtime; determine if O(N) per query is safe.
Implement a segment tree with each node storing (pair count, sorted residual list). Merge two nodes by greedy matching their residuals (small from left, large from right) and concatenating leftovers.
For each query, decompose [L,R] into O(log N) segment tree nodes, merge them left-to-right (which reduces to merging sorted streams), and compute final pair count.
Test the segment-tree solution on Sample 1 and Sample 2 to verify outputs match exactly.

Benchmark segment-tree solution on adversarial inputs (all 1's, 1..N, exponential) with Q=2e5 large queries; if too slow, switch to the optimized two-pointer + precomputed `next[]` approach which is O(R-L+1) per query with tiny constant.
Finalize implementation: write the final Python code enclosed in the required delimiters and ensure it reads from stdin and writes to stdout.
